rows.readmission_bundling_rule: Unplanned 30-day related readmissions are bundled into the original admission; planned returns receive one DRG.

reimbursement_policies.evidence: General inpatient readmission policy applies broadly to inpatient DRG claims, but the requested DRG label is not specifically named. Separate reimbursement is not allowed for unplanned readmissions to the same hospital for the same, similar, or related condition within 30 days, unless an exemption applies.

state_specific_rules: CO Medicaid not subject to this policy
CA: 30 days same or related condition
IN: 3 days same or related problem
exemptions: provider, state, federal, or CMS contracts
transfers from one acute care hospital to another

reimbursement_policies.evidence: The requested DRG is not explicitly listed. This is not a DRG pricing or rate-increase policy; it applies a general inpatient readmission reimbursement rule to acute inpatient claims paid under DRG methodology. Separate reimbursement is generally not allowed for unplanned same, similar, or related readmissions. For the states highlighted in the request, Colorado is exempt from this policy, Indiana uses a 3-day same-or-related standard tied to the first three digits of the principal diagnosis and treats specified-day readmissions as one admission, and California uses a 30-day GBD Standard. Medicare Advantage uses a 30-day same-or-related condition standard.

state_specific_rules: CO: market not subject to this policy
IN: 3-day window; same or related condition based on first three digits of principal diagnosis; specified-day readmissions treated as one admission
Medicare Advantage: 30-day same or related condition standard; same day defined as within 24 hours from discharge to readmission for participating providers
NY: readmissions for multiple trauma treatment excluded
OH: readmissions associated with major trauma excluded
TN: readmissions associated with burns or major trauma excluded
exemptions: Colorado market not subject to policy
transfer to another acute care hospital

recommended_action.description: Recommendation 1: In CA Medicare Advantage DRG readmission editing, keep cesarean/OB delivery admissions carved out from the "30-day window; GBD Standard" because "obstetrical deliveries" are exempt; do not bundle a return stay into the index admission or apply "1 DRG per planned readmission episode" to this OB category. Apply to CA. Exempt: obstetrical deliveries.
